description:
A blazingly fast, lightweight image viewer for Windows powered by Direct2D and SIMD.

QuickView is a high-performance image viewer for Windows, built with Direct2D hardware acceleration
and Google Highway SIMD optimization. It supports 80+ image formats including JPEG XL, AVIF, HEIC,
WebP, and RAW files. Features include HDR display support, portable mode, and GPU-accelerated rendering.
QuickView v6.40.1.1 Stable Release Notes
We are thrilled to announce the official release of QuickView v6.40.1.0 Stable!
This release is the culmination of extensive real-world testing and over two weeks of stability hardening. It introduces our brand-new GeekWidgets atomic UI library, an interactive cropping system and dedicated export panel, native WMF/EMF vector support and dynamic animated SVG playback, direct clipboard bitmap copying, instant loading in folders with 40,000+ files, full keyboard navigation in Settings, and a wide range of important bug fixes.
✨ What's New & How to Use
1. Next-Gen GeekWidgets: Modern Capsule Sliders & Effortless Controls (#144, #242, #243)
We completely re-architected QuickView's custom UI controls with our unified GeekWidgets atomic library, bringing an intuitive, pixel-perfect experience to the Settings overlay:
- Modern Pill Sliders: Replaces clunky legacy sliders with sleek, theme-tinted capsule sliders that feature subtle progress fills and high-contrast accents.
- Vector Steppers (< & >): Dedicated precision stepper buttons at each end allow for single-step adjustments with a single click.
- In-Place Direct Number Input: Click directly on the value text inside the slider to switch into an in-place text input box. Type your desired target value (e.g., 375, 80%, or 1.5) and press Enter—complete with strict boundary checks.
- Quick Reset Button (↺): A standalone reset button next to each slider lets you restore default values in one click.
- Drawing Tablet & Stylus Support: Fully optimized event handling for graphics tablets (e.g., Wacom Intuos), ensuring natural pen scrolling and zero interaction lockups.
2. Interactive Image Cropping & Modern "Save As" Export Panel (#201, #225)
Designed specifically for creators who need quick, zero-friction reframing and saving:
- Enter Crop Mode: Right-click anywhere on the image and select "Crop", or simply press the X hotkey.
- Fast Selection: While in crop mode, hold Ctrl and drag your left mouse button to instantly draw a crop bounding box (Ctrl-drag box selection). Corner and edge handles allow for smooth fine-tuning.
- Dedicated Export Panel: Press Ctrl + S or choose "Save As..." from the context menu to bring up the modern export dialog.
- Modern Formats & Smooth Quality Wheel: Export to JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, or JXL with real-time file size estimation and mouse-wheel quality slider control.
3. Native WMF / EMF Vector Decoding & Animated SVG Support (#242, #238)
- Windows Metafiles (WMF / EMF / WMZ / EMZ): Native, high-performance decoding for classic Windows vector formats with high-quality anti-aliasing and full transparency support.
- Animated SVGs: SVGs utilizing SMIL, CSS animations, or <animateTransform> tags now automatically route through an offscreen host for fluid animation playback, while static vectors retain the blazingly fast Direct2D native rendering pipeline.
4. Direct Clipboard Bitmap Copying (#240)
- Paste Anywhere Seamlessly: Previously, copying an image placed file-drop references (CF_HDROP) on the clipboard, which many third-party apps could not interpret directly.
- How It Works: Press Ctrl + C, and QuickView will generate high-fidelity standard CF_DIBV5 bitmaps via background delayed rendering. You can now immediately paste image pixels directly into Discord, Telegram, Slack, Photoshop, MS Paint, and web editors with Ctrl + V.
5. Instant Opening in Giant Folders (40,000+ Files) (#241)
- Completely revamped the directory indexing and asynchronous scanning pipeline. Opening an image located in a folder with tens of thousands of files is now virtually instantaneous (millisecond-grade startup), eliminating multi-second freezes.
6. Full Keyboard Navigation in Settings (#144)
- 100% Mouse-Free Control: Navigate the entire settings overlay seamlessly using Tab, Shift + Tab, Arrow keys, Enter, and Space.
🐛 Bug Fixes
- [#246] Window Exit Focus Handover: Fixed an issue where closing QuickView failed to return keyboard focus cleanly to the preceding application or the desktop.
- [#243] Tablet Scrolling in Settings: Resolved an issue where Wacom Intuos and stylus pens were unable to scroll the settings view.
- [#242] Gallery & Slider Glitches:
  - Fixed an issue where exiting the thumbnail gallery opened via the context menu erroneously closed the currently viewed image;
  - Fixed a boundary threshold bug where the gallery would fail to launch when the window width was under 377px;
  - Fixed stepped value jumping on the minimum window size slider.
- [#241] Severe Freeze in Huge Directories: Resolved long startup delays and UI locks when opening files in directories containing tens of thousands of images.
- [#240] Cross-App Paste Limitations: Added standard DIB bitmap clipboard streaming so copied images can be pasted anywhere.
- [#238] SVG Text & CJK Missing: Fixed text elements and flowcharts disappearing or rendering as blank canvases on specific complex SVG files.
- [#234] Settings Tag Cloud Hit-Testing: Fixed an issue where info panel configuration buttons became unclickable at specific UI scales.
- [#144] Window Resize Flickering: Eliminated UI flicker and jitter when dragging window borders, and blocked double-click events from leaking through overlays and edge-nav hotspots.
- [#201 / #225] Crop Pipeline Polish: Fixed an infinite prompt loop on crop exit and ensured DComp surfaces and info panel dimensions synchronize accurately upon applying crops.
❤️ Special Thanks
We want to extend our heartfelt gratitude to the community members and contributors who made this release possible:
- Dmitry Yerokhin (@Dimmitrius) for PR #251, thoroughly reviewing, fixing, and polishing the entire Russian localization.
- Our active community reporters who provided detailed reproduction steps and test assets
